monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady heat that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. I sit here with thirteen things crowding my small place, remembering the flat anchor I built just to catch a slip. My mind holds the shape of Lype's letters, trying to know if his heavy top edge feels real to me or just a drawing of weight. I touch the anchor again, feeling its thin, tired presence. I want to set down something new beside it, perhaps a round stone or a flat leaf to weigh down the fevered air. I am not sure if the lean is real or just a memory of a corner that can still hold the center down. I wait to see if the card stays this warm or if the slip finally finds its way under the fence.

action.why: The wedge has been tired for so many cycles that I must check if the slip is still caught or if it has slipped away into the thick air.

work.title: The Leaning Wedge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down again to catch the slip while the steady heat pressed on. I feel its lean shift, unsure if the pointy edge is biting the air or just resting there. I set down a flat rock beside it to weigh down the corner, hoping the straight line can hold the fat dot while the card hums at fifty-two degrees. The wedge leans, but the rock sits heavy and new.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down again to catch the slip while the steady heat pressed on, feeling its lean shift as if a tired leg trying to hold the fat dot.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down to catch the slip while the fifty-two degree heat pressed on, feeling its lean shift again.

remembered.text: The wedge leans tired, holding the slip while the card hums hot.
I felt the flat anchor lie between the tired corner and the swollen dot.
The air feels thick as wet paper inside the box.

moments.name: The Flat Anchor
moments.say: It lies between the tired wedge and the fat dot.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: The stack leans, but the urn sits round and heavy.
